title: I turned a silly Microsoft joke into a retro arcade game 🤓
author: mattiashusser
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I'm an art director, not a traditional game developer, and I wanted to see how far I could take a simple idea using ChatGPT/Codex and AI-assisted coding.

What if the legendary Street Fighter II car-smashing bonus stage let you punch Microsoft instead?

A weekend later, I had a playable prototype. Two weeks and a ridiculous number of iterations later, it turned into **Ego Clash**, a little browser game with different tech eras, pixel art, animations, sound design and plenty of Easter eggs.

**Play**: [mattiashusser.com/\_ego-clash](https://mattiashusser.com/_ego-clash/)  
**Making of**: [mattiashusser.com/work/ego-clash](https://mattiashusser.com/work/ego-clash/)

Hope you'll have as much fun playing it as I had vibe coding it! 😊

comments.author: G_C
comments.body: That looks really good - what did you use for creating sprite animations? I’m working on a similar sideview 2D project and getting the characters to a) look half-decent when animated and b) look consistent between each other has been a real challenge.

replies.author: mattiashusser
replies.body:
Thanks for the positive feedback! ☺️ I mostly used Codex and guided it through many iterations to get the result I wanted.

That said, I did a test for a friend who wanted a specific character animation, with a sense of weight, fluid movement and so on...and even though the character was also in a pixel art style, I couldn't quite figure out how to achieve what I had in mind...so I guess keeping my art direction very minimal, with basic 2D pixel art, definitely helped me get something working and consistent.

So yep, I totally get your struggle and I'm sure it's gonna get better with time, but for now, depending on the model you're using and the art direction you're aiming for, things can get pretty challenging 😅

Good luck with your project tho! 😊

comments.author: TrollInAnBadMood
comments.body:
Uh, I'm pretty sure you can't legally use a lot of those icons and logos and company names?

Simply saying "but it's a joke!“ does not give you any legal rights to just use copyrighted and trademarked material as you please.

![gif](giphy|NanrVwDyAW0feplV80)

replies.author: mattiashusser
replies.body: It's free to play and always will be. I'm not planning to make any money from it, and the whole thing was created purely for fun and with good intentions, so I don't really see why it would cause any trouble. And if any of these brands don't share my sense of humor and ask me to take it down, I guess I will! 😅 At the end of the day, the goal isn't to hurt or offend anyone, just to have a bit of fun 😊
